cassandra-mi-nodes-multiple-of-3.title: Node count is not a multiple of 3
cassandra-mi-nodes-multiple-of-3.body: Microsoft recommends the number of nodes per datacenter be a multiple of the replication factor (3), so 3, 6, 9... Uneven counts leave data unevenly spread. Confirm the node count or round it to a multiple of 3.

citation.source: Best practices for optimal performance in Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra
citation.quote: We also recommend that you specify a multiple of the replication factor as the number of nodes.

cassandra-mi-production-small-nodes.title: Nodes under 16 cores for production
cassandra-mi-production-small-nodes.body: This production estimate uses Cassandra nodes with fewer than 16 cores. Microsoft says most workloads need at least 16 cores to perform properly. Confirm the workload is small, or price a larger node size.

citation.source: Best practices for optimal performance in Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra
citation.quote: Most workloads need a minimum of 16 cores to perform properly.

cassandra-mi-few-disks.title: Fewer than 4 data disks per node
cassandra-mi-few-disks.body: Microsoft strongly recommends at least four P30 disks on each Cassandra node. Fewer disks give less storage and less disk throughput per node.

citation.source: Quickstart: Create an Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra cluster from the Azure portal
citation.quote: Select the number of P30 disks to attach to each Cassandra node (a minimum of four is strongly recommended).
